body:
**Draft — this is for looking at, not for merging.** Opened so the icons can be built and seen in the running app rather than judged from a folder of files. Discussion: #689.

**Browsable gallery** (each icon beside the current one, plus true 16/22/32 px renders):
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/bef8f7fd-d9aa-4608-9f9d-ef7ffbca1a1d

## What this is

88 SVG icons for the QET-specific concepts that no general icon theme contains — conductors, terminals, terminal strips, folios, cross-references, terminal orientation marks, conductor end styles, element master/slave links, title blocks.

Matching all 183 icon names against the current upstream Breeze tree (7,107 names) gives **93 hits and 90 misses**. The misses are precisely the electrical concepts, and no upstream will ever carry them. #687 covers vendoring the 93 that already exist upstream; this covers the remainder.

## Why drawn, rather than traced or generated

- **Autotracing** the existing 16–22 px bitmaps would turn their anti-aliasing into permanent bézier wobble — a scalable icon that still looks bad.
- **Image generators** emit raster, so it would need tracing anyway, and they do not hold stroke weight or optical size across a set.

These are simple technical symbols: a terminal is a rectangle and a stub, a conductor is a polyline. That is path data, not illustration.

## The spec was measured, not invented

`#4d4d4d` is the dominant stroke colour across QET's current icons. The terminal red/blue split came from sampling `ico/22x22/terminal.png` (80% red, 20% blue).

Semantics are preserved — red = phase, blue = neutral, green = earth is electrical convention, not decoration — while the values are harmonised onto the Breeze palette so these sit correctly beside the 93 stock icons they share a toolbar with. A mixed toolbar was assembled to check this, and the two sets are hard to tell apart.

Coherence is structural rather than a matter of care: one `badge_new()` serves every "add" icon, the four stacking-order icons and the five conductor end styles are each generated by a single function, and the four orientation marks are one drawing rotated.

## Incidental fix

`ConductorSettings`, `DiagramAdd` and `DiagramDelete` each carried **different artwork at 16 px and 22 px** — `conductor-reset` vs `conductor2`, `folio-new` vs `diagram_add`, `folio-delete` vs `diagram_del`. Collapsing each to one scalable file resolves that.

Also `simplifyrichtext` was loaded by a direct `QIcon(":/ico/32x32/…")` in `richtexteditor.cpp` rather than through the registry; that call site is updated too.

## Verified

- Builds clean, CMake/Ninja Release, Qt 5.15 — 820/820, links.
- Runs under Xvfb with **no resource or icon-engine warnings**; the new glyphs render in the real toolbar.
- All 84 wired resource paths resolve to files on disk.
- `ico/copyright` gains a stanza for `ico/scalable/*` recording these as GPL-2+ and **not** derived from Breeze artwork.

## Deliberately not done

- **Superseded PNGs are left in place.** The change stays additive and trivially revertible; deleting them is follow-up work.
- **The 93 stock Breeze icons are untouched** — that is #687's job, and it should not be entangled with this.
- **`project-delete.svg` was dropped** from the branch: nothing in the tree references that asset.

## Honest limits

**The eight icons previously flagged as needing another pass have been redrawn** — `autoconnect`, `item-move`, `export-csv`, `run-dxf`, `folder-only-this` and the three properties icons. None carries a flag now. The properties mark in particular was tried twice as a corner badge before being moved inside the shape: at the ~12 px a badge gets, detail collapses to a smudge whatever sits behind it.

**Optical sizing was audited by measurement, not by eye.** Rendering every icon and measuring its real ink extents found ink running 10–22 wide and 2–20 tall, 30 icons off-centre, and 18 breaching a 1 px safe margin — three clipped at the canvas edge. One cause was invisible in the source: `stroke-linejoin="miter"` on the stacking-order parallelograms threw a spike past the nominal geometry. All four counts are now zero.

**The existing stacking-order icons are arguably cleaner than these replacements.** The gain there is HiDPI rendering, not aesthetics.

Most importantly: **this is one contributor's judgement on legibility, not a user's on whether the metaphors are right.** That is the part that needs other eyes, and the reason this is a draft rather than a merge request. If the direction is unwanted, saying so now costs nothing — the generator is a script, and the set can be regenerated to a different spec.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Fq6v5jnifdpcwCoPocrp6e

commits.messageBody:
Drawing to a stroke spec keeps the *weight* uniform but not the optical
*size*: each glyph still ended up whatever size its own geometry happened to
be. Measured across all 88 icons against the 22px canvas:

  ink width   10 - 22   (median 18)
  ink height   2 - 20   (median 16)
  off-centre by more than 0.5px : 30 icons
  ink outside a 1px safe margin : 18 icons
  undersized (largest side < 13): 1

In a toolbar that reads as "the sizes are wrong" -- orientation marks at 14x11
sitting beside folio icons at 20x20.

Four causes, all fixed at the source rather than per icon:

- Badges (new/delete/edit/properties) were placed at 16,16 with +-4 offsets;
  with a 2px stroke that reached x=21, and badge_props' backing ran to x=22 on
  a 22px canvas. Moved to 15,15 and tightened.
- Export arrows, the stacking-order arrow, the eye in masquer/restaurer, and
  view_fit_width's arrows all ran into or past the canvas edge.
- The stacking-order parallelograms used stroke-linejoin="miter". Acute
  corners throw a miter spike well past the nominal geometry, which is what
  pushed that family's ink to x=0. Changed to round.
- endline-none was a bare 10x2 stem against a set median of 18x16 and read as
  a stray dash; it now spans the same width its siblings occupy.

Remaining centring was corrected by wrapping each drawing in a translate()
computed from its measured ink box. Translation only, never scale: scaling a
group scales its stroke widths too, which would defeat the uniform 2px weight
the spec exists to guarantee.

tools/icon-audit/normalise_icons.py in the harness repo performs the audit by
rendering and measuring rather than parsing path data, and is idempotent -- an
existing translate wrapper is replaced, not nested, so re-running cannot drift
an icon.

After: 0 off-centre, 0 undersized, 0 oversized, 0 breaching the safe margin.
The residual height spread is inherent to linear shapes -- a horizontal
conductor line is 2px tall and cannot be otherwise.

Rebuilt clean and re-checked under Xvfb; the toolbar now reads at a consistent
optical size.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Normalise optical sizing and centring across the icon set

commits.messageBody:
Each was noted as weak in the gallery rather than quietly shipped. All eight
now read correctly and stay legible at 16px.

autoconnect      A lightning bolt above two stubs dominated the glyph and read
                 as "power" rather than "connect". Now shows what the feature
                 does: two terminals with the conductor QET routes between
                 them, drawn in the accent colour to mark it as generated.

item-move        A square with one diagonal arrow reads as *resize*. The item
                 now carries the same four-way cross i_move() uses.

export-csv       A single horizontal and vertical rule did not read as a
                 spreadsheet. Now a header band and a real row/column grid,
                 which also separates it from export-pdf's red band.

run-dxf          An X in a box reads as "no". Now a drawing file -- the CAD
                 geometry DXF actually carries -- plus the run arrow.

folder-only-this Two faint dashes did not read as "the other folders". The
                 excluded ones are now drawn as folders, greyed back.

folio-properties, project-properties, folder-properties
                 The properties mark was tried twice as a corner badge: bare
                 rails, then rails on a disc. At the ~12px a badge gets, the
                 rails collapse to a grey smudge whatever sits behind them.
                 Moved inside the shape, where they get the full width and
                 stay readable -- which is what QET's existing icons already
                 did. badge_props() is gone, replaced by props_rows().

Re-audited after the redraw: 0 off-centre, 0 undersized, 0 oversized, 0
breaching the safe margin. Rebuilt clean.
